To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the protein kinase C-activated Ca2+ channel in UMR-106 osteoblast-like cells is a voltage-independent, high-threshold Ca2+ channel that is sensitive to the dihydropyridine Ca2+ channel antagonists nicardipine, nifedipine, and verapamil, but is insensitive to the phenylalkylamine Ca2+ channel antagonist verapamil and the dihydropiridine Ca2+ channel agonist BAYK864
the protein kinase C-activated Ca2+ channel is a Ca2+-selective, voltage-dependent, nicardipine-sensitive Ca2+ channel.
protein kinase C stimulation in the UMR-106 cell line results in the activation of a Ca2+ channel that is dependent on medium Ca2+ for its activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the cytosolic free Ca2+ concentration in osteoblastic cells.
the characterization of a protein kinase C-activated Ca2+ channel in UMR-106 osteoblast-like cells.
the characterization of the protein kinase-C-activated Ca2+ channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein kinase C-activated Ca2+ channel is similar but distinct from PTH-activated Ca2+-channel in UMR-106 cell line.

protein kinase C-activated Ca2+ channels in osteoblasts are similar to the cAMP-dependent PTH-stimulating Ca2+ channels, with respect to their activation and inhibition by various agents, but are different in terms of the kinetics of the response and their sensitivity to the Ca2+ antagonist.

protein kinase C-activated Ca2+ channels are similar to those activated by PTH and forskolin, except that the protein kinase C- activated channels are more sensitive to inhibition by protein kinase C activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are at least two different types of cAMP-independent Ca2+ channels in these cells.
the protein kinase C-activated Ca2+ channel is similar to the cAMP-dependent channel with the exception of the lag period and sensitivity to PTH.
protein kinase C- and PTH-induced Ca2+ channels have similar properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the protein kinase C-induced Ca2+ channel is a distinct entity from the PTH-stimulatd Ca2+ channel.
the protein kinase C-activated Ca2+ channel is similar to the PTH-activated Ca2+-permeable channel.
protein kinase C activation results in the opening of a Ca2+ channel in the osteosarcoma-like clonal osteoblast UMR-106 cell line.
